scores.q: Q1 representable (what it is, how it stands, why it matters, from where they land)
scores.why: How it stands is unusually well told in 616 words: 505 of 536 receipts and what they do not show, no central result new mathematics, no human review, ethics on two unasserted premises, frozen predictions mostly failed. What it is comes in two unconnected pieces, a proxy-problem result and then 'an account of how anything comes to be', and 'In plain words' is not plain after its first sentence. Why it matters is missing: the first screen has 0 uses of 'alignment' and 'coordination', and does not say what is left once the mathematics is not new. It also never says the work was written with AI, which the one page says in its first paragraph. The next page, the one page, is dense for a newcomer: 'The root' paragraph and the T7 table cell.
scores.to_reach_8: _process/navigation/README-FIRST-SCREEN.md: (1) add the authorship clause without the token the test bans, e.g. 'written with language models, the Lean proofs included'. (2) Rewrite 'In plain words' as short sentences that keep the qualifiers: one for the problem, one per result, with 'a rule read from the share of its own winners' replaced by an example. (3) Join 'An account' to that lead in one sentence saying the selection results are the part of the general account a reader can use first. (4) Add one 'why it matters' sentence stating the purpose (predict, share understanding, coordinate; alignment of trained systems) and what survives, copied from ONE-PAGE: 'a ledger of premises, each shown holding in one model and failing in another, and an ethics with scope and order apart'. (5) Define 'grammar' in a clause. theories/becoming/ONE-PAGE.md: mark a ten-minute part, as AGENTS asks of fronts, and shorten the T7 cell, its full standing being in chapter 02. Check every restatement against its home with a second reader.

The connection map is the best object in the project. Faithful: pages are converted from the repository and leaving links are pinned to the commit. Two things hold it down. The home is the README's first screen as HTML, eight paragraphs of text before the picture and the cards, so the site gains little from being a site. A 667-page site has no search; I found no search input on the pages I grepped and no search rules in site.css. Not reachable yet: no public URL exists.

findings.where: Title 生成变化之论 in README.zh.md, ONE-PAGE.zh.md, the overview; GLOSSARY.zh.md line 35
findings.problem: The project's Chinese name uses 生成, which the glossary reserves for one branch: a pattern going on through renewal, which excludes 退化 (生成与守各自排除退化), and the glossary warns it is neither 生起 nor 生生. The account covers ceasing and degeneration and assumes none of it good, so the name suggests generation. The body meanwhile renders becoming as 生灭变化 (README.zh 1, ONE-PAGE.zh 2, overview 6), and the glossary has no entry for the name or for 生灭变化. A reader will take the title as a theory of generating, close to the misreading the project keeps correcting.
findings.fix: Decide the name by argument: keep it with an explicit gloss in the first paragraph and a glossary entry saying its 生成 is not chapter 02's 生成, or rename to 生灭变化之论 for consistency with the body. Whichever is chosen, use one term for becoming across all zh fronts.

read: Read in full: README.zh.md, theories/becoming/ONE-PAGE.zh.md, THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.zh.md, USES.zh.md, review/README.zh.md, results/THEORY-GRAPH.zh.md, results/atlas/CROSSWALK.zh.md. Read the first 157 lines of the English README.md (first screen, opening, notes), and the openings of RESULTS.md and ONE-PAGE.md for comparison. Read in part: USES-EXAMPLES.zh.md (head, fishers, start of the judge audit, valley, 天之道); LINEAGE.zh.md (header, 简述, start of the thread, first rows of turning points, renames, folders); chapter 06 (opening through §一 and §十一; outline of the rest; the English-free middle not read); GLOSSARY.zh.md (opening rows and targeted entries); review/CLASSICAL-TEXTS.md (first paragraphs); experiments/direction-installation/README.md (head); .github/workflows/pages.yml. Searched only, not read: other chapters, TESTS.md body, the rest of the glossary. Looked at as rendered with headless Chrome, not on a device: zh home and LINEAGE at desktop, zh home and USES in 390 px frames, spine.zh.svg. The lineage picture was viewed; connections.html was not opened. A script checked link targets and anchors on nine zh site pages (0 broken of the internal links, 564 anchors resolved) and counted zh-versus-English destinations. Comparison of zh against English wording was by reading sampled passages, not a line-by-line audit; I found no factual divergence in what I compared beyond the caption note. Whether github.io is reachable from mainland China is general knowledge, not tested. No tests run, nothing edited in the tree; screenshots are in the scratchpad only. Overall for a Chinese reader: honest, well-labelled and far ahead of the 7 November scores, with USES at 8; the distance to 8 elsewhere is mainly Chinese that reads as Chinese, a Chinese view of the tests, and putting 古文 where this reader lands.

scores.q: Q1. How representable is the project
scores.why: From either landing a newcomer gets what it is, a real case, what it is for, the ethics' two premises and an unusually candid standing (505 of 536 receipts, none of the central results new mathematics, no human review), in 476 words. Two things hold it below 8. The first paragraph is hard going: 'one side of the proxy problem, as a reading, its blindness to what a measure does not register'; 'a rule read from the share of its own winners, favouring them, locks on them'. And on GitHub the first screen runs straight into the full 24-note first-person opening, so the four-layer reading path comes only after about 68 KB.
scores.to_reach_8: (1) README.md, through _process/research-config.json readme_first_screen: split the first paragraph's two long sentences and move 'as a reading' into a following sentence; put 'An account of...' first or merge it, so sentence one says what the thing is. (2) tools/research/research.py with the readme_lead/readme_opening keys: insert a short 'Ways in' table (the site's ways_in cards from research-config.json) between the spine caption and '## Truth exists', or replace the inline opening with a link to theories/becoming/OPENING.md, which already holds it. (3) Say what 'Lean' is once on the first screen: a proof checker.

scores.q: Q2. Is there a static website
scores.why: As built it is good. It has 667 HTML pages from an allow-list, a footer naming the commit, a sticky nav on every page, light and dark themes, a text column that holds at phone width (viewed in a 390 px frame), and an interactive connection map. My link pass found 0 missing internal targets and 0 bad anchors. But it is not reachable until the switch is thrown. With 667 pages it has no search. Generated pages show two navs at once (the site bar plus the 15-link GitHub line, seen on RESULTS and TESTS). 'Ways in', the page's real navigation, sits below about two and a half screens of hero text and spine picture. The map's prose still says 'once the reader's site is published' on the published site.
scores.to_reach_8: (1) tools/publishing/build_site.py: strip the '[Home](...) · [Where everything is]...' line from pages that get the site header. (2) Same builder: render the ways_in section directly after the 'Start with' paragraph and before the spine image, or add an 'All ways in' anchor link at the top of the hero. (3) Add a small static client-side search over page titles and record names (a generated JSON index); the site then needs no server. (4) MAP.md and CROSSWALK.md: have the builder drop the 'once the reader's site is published... GitHub shows only its source' clauses on the site. (5) What the switch adds: a public URL, one working map link in place of a 4.9 MB source view, and the README can then link the site from its first line. That link should be added at the same time in readme_first_screen.

scores.q: Q3. Are the unification and connections shown elegantly
scores.why: spine.svg is legible and keeps edge kinds apart (formal-reuse solid, interpretive dashed, application dotted, spokes counting modules, related-for-analogy named as not drawn). It states '11 derived, 1 under a stated hypothesis, 6 counting, 99 at a named distance' at the top of the picture itself, which is the honest limit on unification. The connection map adds a separate view with filters by relation and an agreement-of-law versus agreement-of-reading split, and says 'every thread an AI reading'.
scores.to_reach_8: Already 8. To go higher: the spine as an has no click-through on GitHub, so add under the README and ONE-PAGE picture a one-line list linking each chapter number 01–08 to its file. Also add a text link 'which 117' from the spine caption to the table at THEORY-GRAPH.md#the-spine.

scores.q: Q4. Is it clear how the whole grew
scores.why: theories/LINEAGE.md opens with six phases in brief, each counting who wrote what states it, then lineage.svg (shape for what states it, fill for who wrote it, the selection thread drawn through), and states 14–18 minutes for that part. It is in the nav line, on the first-screen caption and on a home card. I read its head and picture, and did not read the 48 points row by row.
scores.to_reach_8: Already 8. Polish: the picture's labelled points thin out in the last phase (only point 45 is titled in 'Tests, editions, crosswalk'), though that is where the account's standing changed most; title one or two more in theories/becoming/results/data/lineage.json.

scores.q: Q5. Can people understand what value it provides
scores.why: The value claim is early, the concrete case is real and its failure is stated ('frozen predictions mostly failed'), and 'No test designed from it has yet run on a deployed pipeline' guards against overclaim. The gap is on the landing itself. It tells the reader none of the central results is new mathematics and never says what is valuable given that. The answer exists one page in, in ONE-PAGE.md's evidence paragraph: 'a ledger of premises, each shown holding in one model and failing in another, and an ethics with scope and order apart'. 'What it is for' is four abstract questions with no statement of what a user would do differently.
scores.to_reach_8: (1) readme_first_screen, in the 'Lean receipts' paragraph directly after 'known result restated': add the ONE-PAGE sentence on what survives, copied from its home in chapters/08-METHOD.md#known-results. (2) In 'What it is for': add one concrete clause from USES-EXAMPLES.md#auditing-a-language-model-judge saying what the audit found on that judge, so the four questions are seen answering something.

scores.q: Q6. Does it clearly show how it can be used in fields
scores.why: USES.md is a field-by-field table with what you can do today, how it stands and what is not claimed; 'Nothing claimed' opens the human-development row, and the alignment, people-and-AI, coordination, human-development, wisdom-traditions and sciences fields each have worked examples in USES-EXAMPLES.md, labelled at their standing. USES.md links its examples by anchor 11 times. I read USES.md's head and table rows (the long rows cut off) and the examples page's outline, not each example through.
scores.to_reach_8: Already 8. To go higher: MAP.md's 'Where to start' does not link USES-EXAMPLES.md at all; add it beside the USES link. USES.md's nav lacks a link back to the home page.

scores.q: Q7. Are valuable things easy to see, and their connections clear
scores.why: Strong base: on the site every valuable page is one click from home by a card, and on GitHub the 15-link line reaches all named pages. No front exceeds 1 MB (the largest chapter is 270 KB, RESULTS 175 KB, README 87 KB). Front-page links and anchors checked clean; the 138 LINEAGE hits are ?plain=1 line links my check does not parse, and I did not confirm their targets. But the nav line exists only on generated pages. The pages newcomers actually reach first (ONE-PAGE, USES, OPENING, the overview, MAP, GLOSSARY, theories/README, review README, CROSSWALK, chapters/README) have partial or no nav and no Home link. Results opens on an alphabetical 536-row table starting 'a-cascade-at-the-histories-reached'. Open questions leads with neither the crux nor the question the README calls first. Lean checking, the main thing a sceptic wants, is not one click from the GitHub first screen.
scores.to_reach_8: (1) Inject the same nav line into MAP.md, GLOSSARY.md, theories/README.md, theories/becoming/ONE-PAGE.md, USES.md, USES-EXAMPLES.md, OPENING.md, THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md, review/README.md, chapters/README.md and results/atlas/CROSSWALK.md, via the generators where one exists and a shared include for the rest. (2) RESULTS.md (research.py render): open with a 'Start here' block linking the 117 central declarations (THEORY-GRAPH.md#the-spine and 08 §7) and add a chapter column or group by chapter. (3) OPEN-QUESTIONS.md: open with the crux (07-SIGNIFICANCE.md#crux), the step and the warrant of C, then the registered targets; and move 'Discovery and evidence' and 'Preserved history' off the reader's page. (4) Add 'Check the proofs' (MAP.md#check-the-proofs-yourself) to the shared nav line and to the 'Lean receipts' paragraph of readme_first_screen.

scores.q: Q1. How representable is the project

scores.q: Q1. How representable is the project
scores.why: The home at site-r3/index.html says what the project is, gives one case, and states its standing with unusual candour: 505 of 536 Lean receipts, none of the central results new mathematics, no human review, predictions mostly failed. Two things hold it back. The opening paragraph is qualifier-dense ('one side of the proxy problem, as a reading, its blindness to what a measure does not register'), so a newcomer gets the hedges before the point. The English home also never says the account was made with AI, while the Chinese home and the one page do.

scores.q: Q2. Is there a static website
scores.why: Built: 667 HTML pages from an allow-list that refuses private paths. My own audit found 0 broken internal links or anchors among those pages. It has calm typography, a dark-mode palette (read in the CSS, not rendered), a sound 375px layout, relative links that suit a project-pages URL, and a footer naming the commit and each page's source. It is not reachable yet. It also lacks what a real way in needs: no contents on chapters of 2 to 6.5 hours, no search, no 404 page or favicon, duplicate navigation on 6 pages, and clipped wide tables. Two pages print a local home path. The switch would add only a public URL, and the README and MAP.md do not yet name any site URL.

scores.q: Q3. Are unification and connections shown elegantly
scores.why: The honesty is strong. spine.svg prints 11 derived, 1 under a hypothesis, 6 counting and 99 at a named distance above the picture. It keeps formal-reuse, interpretive and application edges apart. connections.html opens with a 14.2% and 3.2% error estimate, offers filters by relation, and 'The root's reach' is a clear bar view. The drawing is weaker. Spine curves overlap in the centre so no single path can be followed, and the picture is an whose chapter circles do not link. The 'Graph' page repeats the same picture over static tables of a 3,220-node graph. The loom opens as a tangle until a reader selects something.
